The hybrid option provides balance but should not receive automatic preference without agreed criteria.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"agent_1","position":"Favors option A: spending the full budget on an inter-city tournament, buffet, and prizes to increase club visibility.","influence":0.33},{"agent":"agent_2","position":"Favors option B: investing the full budget in educational materials and new chessboards; this position won the debate, though only moderately.","influence":0.4},{"agent":"agent_3","position":"Favors option C: splitting the budget equally between a smaller tournament and equipment as a compromise.","influence":0.27}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"The disagreement concerns competing but legitimate goals rather than incompatible principles. Use a scored or ranked social-choice process with jointly agreed criteria, such as measurable outreach, participant benefit, durability, and implementation feasibility. Option C is a reasonable provisional compromise, but the group should consider a data-informed allocation or pilot with evaluation metrics rather than an arbitrary equal split."}
